SEC25A-01.note: Plural subject 'Cattle' plus present tense set by 'provided that ... comes'. 'were safe' tempts via the past 'was screened' in the first sentence.

SEC25A-02.note: 'Each X and Y' takes a singular verb; past tense from 'before the growers recognized'. The compound subject and the plural 'trays' next to the blank pull toward 'were developing'.

SEC25A-03.note: Singular head 'comparison'; a specific past time ('on the third day of that year's monsoon') rules out the present perfect. 'candidates' next to the blank attracts the plural options.

SEC25A-04.note: Elliptical auxiliary must echo 'has withstood' -> plural 'have not [withstood]'. 'do not' is attractive as a general-truth ellipsis but does not match the perfect verb being elided.

SEC25A-05.convention: pronoun reference: 'their' can take 'nurses' (the outreach team's own vaccine refrigerator) as antecedent
SEC25A-05.note: Verb agrees with 'nurses' (have moved); intended pronoun is 'its' for the clinic. But 'their' has a grammatical plural antecedent (nurses) and the reading that the team moved its own refrigerator is coherent; 'its' itself is ambiguous among clinic/hospital/program.

SEC25A-06.note: 'health workers' -> carry; only the cholera vaccine is heat-stable, so 'it'. 'them' tempts via 'three oral vaccines'.

SEC25A-07.note: Singular 'Contact dermatitis' + intransitive 'recurred' requires 'has'; 'is/are recurred' are impossible passives. 'patches'/'wrists' in the appositive pull toward 'have'.

SEC25A-08.note: Blood came from all four barns, so 'drawn in the barn nearest the duck pond' is restrictive: no punctuation. The comma before 'where' makes 'samples, drawn' look like the opener of a nonessential pair; 'drawn,' splitting participle from its phrase is rejectable on sight.

SEC25B-01.note: Singular 'atlas', present tense from 'if a fragment ... turns out'. 'trails' adjacent to the blank attracts the plural.

SEC25B-02.note: Plural 'mains'; specific past time 'at the height of last winter's cold snap' excludes the present perfect. 'reservoir'/'hospital' singular attractors.

SEC25B-03.note: Singular 'seismometer', present progressive matching 'while ... scientists ... sort out'. 'aftershocks' next to the blank attracts the plural.

SEC25B-04.note: 'survey teams' -> are sampling; the emissions are the lone active vent's -> 'its'. 'their' tempts via 'universities'/'older craters', but the older craters are not active.

SEC25B-05.note: Ellipsis of present 'discharge' after a singular subject separated by an appositive -> 'does not'. The past-tense first and last sentences ('gauged', 'came') make 'was not' attractive; 'do not' tempts via 'springs'/'edge' proximity.

SEC25B-06.note: Singular 'glare', past from 'struck'. 'panels' attracts plural; the present 'track' inside the relative clause attracts 'is'.

SEC25B-07.note: Compound subject 'a technician and two engineers' -> were; the object is the dish -> 'it'. 'them' tempts via 'wind farms'.

SEC25B-08.note: Two independent clauses ('...left a jagged scar' / 'a crescent ... drew climbers') need a semicolon. Comma and colon both invite an appositive reading of 'a crescent of bare rock' until 'drew' strands; a colon is weakly defensible only if the second clause elaborated the first, which it does not. Bare 'scar a' is struck on sight.

SEC25C-01.note: Compound 'the fresco and the gilded screen' -> plural; present from 'unless ... are moved'. 'chancel' singular attractor.

SEC25C-02.note: Singular 'rivalry', present from 'after the judges have read out'. 'bands' attracts plural; the past narrative ('founded', 'outlived') attracts 'was'.

SEC25C-03.note: Singular 'portrait', bounded past period ('during the decades after the painters' deaths') -> simple past, and present perfect would imply it is still obscure, contradicting 'Scholars have begun to study it'. 'sisters' attracts plural.

SEC25C-04.note: 'townspeople' -> were; they defended the cathedral/porch -> 'its'. 'their' tempts by number-matching the subject and via 'canons'.

SEC25C-05.note: Singular 'restorer' (appositive intervening) -> has; the object is 'frescoes' -> 'them'. 'it' tempts via 'apse'/'whitewash'.

SEC25C-06.note: Ellipsis of 'was structurally sound' with plural head 'remains' -> 'were not'. 'tower' singular attracts 'was not'; 'have not' has no auxiliary to echo.

SEC25C-07.note: Singular 'chapel' -> was; agent is 'the choir monks' -> 'them'. 'stalls' attracts 'were'; 'it' tempts via 'upper church'. The passive with 'by them' is stilted.

SEC25C-08.note: Two copyists ('two distinct hands', 'Both men') -> plural possessive copyists'. 'Each orchestral part ... a hired copyist' makes the singular possessive attractive.

SEC25D-01.note: Ellipsis of 'are eligible' with plural 'the elderly' -> 'are not'. 'is not' tempts if 'the elderly' is read as a singular collective; 'have not' has no auxiliary to echo.

SEC25D-02.note: Singular 'eye tracker' -> follows; the eyes are the infants' -> 'their'. 'its' tempts by number-matching the subject.

SEC25D-03.note: A direct question ('which language should the merged school teach') ends with a question mark before the new sentence. Period tempts as the plain sentence break; 'teach most' fused is rejectable on sight.

SEC25D-04.note: Plural 'applications', past from 'reached'. 'employer' singular attractor; present perfect conflicts with the past conditional.

SEC25D-05.note: Plural 'assignments', past from 'voted'. 'crews' is plural too, so the singular attractor is weak ('charter'/'commission' earlier).

SEC25D-06.note: Singular 'archivist' -> is converting; the tapes -> 'them'. 'it' tempts via 'trunk'/'museum'.

SEC25D-07.note: Singular 'bookkeeper' (long appositive) -> was entering; names and amounts are the borrowers' -> 'their'. 'its' tempts via 'lender' and number-matching the subject.

SEC25D-08.note: 'voters never changed mayors' means one mayor across the twelve years -> singular possessive mayor's. The plural 'mayors' printed in the passage makes 'mayors'' attractive; the cue is an inference, not a grammatical signal.

tells: Pronoun+verb 2x2 grids: in all ten (SEC25A-05, SEC25A-06, SEC25B-04, SEC25B-07, SEC25C-04, SEC25C-05, SEC25C-07, SEC25D-02, SEC25D-06, SEC25D-07) the key's pronoun number is the OPPOSITE of its verb number (plural verb + its/it, or singular verb + their/them). A test-taker who gets the verb right can pick the mismatched pronoun without finding the antecedent; the two 'matched' options never win.

Present perfect (has been / have been) is never the key in any tense x number grid where it appears (SEC25A-03, SEC25B-02, SEC25C-03, SEC25D-04, SEC25D-05); deleting the two perfect options leaves a coin flip on number.

Agreement items always place an opposite-number noun immediately before the blank (trays, candidates, trails, aftershocks, panels, chancel, bands, sisters, employer), so 'pick the number opposite to the adjacent noun' finds the key's number in nearly every agreement item.

Elliptical items (SEC25A-04, SEC25B-05, SEC25C-06, SEC25D-01): the key always repeats the auxiliary/tense of the earlier verb in the same sentence; 'have not' / 'do not' alternatives lose unless they echo it.
The batch is dominated by one shape (~28 of 32 are subject-verb agreement and/or pronoun with a 2x2 or 2x2+tense grid); only SEC25A-08, SEC25B-08, SEC25D-03 test punctuation.
